motivation: Simple annual and smoothed sea-ice-duration predictors and an annual snowfall-by-habitat interaction do not explain the common decline plus local heterogeneity. Test a biologically distinct terrestrial state variable: within-island breeding-colony network structure.
ecological_hypothesis: Loss and concentration of occupied breeding subcolonies represent erosion of usable terrestrial breeding habitat; lower colony-network diversity at census year t should predict more negative island population growth from t to t+1, beyond current abundance and secular time trend.

data.colony_unit: colony_code within island and census year

predictor.primary: effective_colony_number_t = 1 / sum_j(p_jt^2), where p_jt is colony j share of positive island breeding pairs at year t
predictor.transform: log1p(effective_colony_number_t), standardized using training rows within each LOYO fold
predictor.direction: positive coefficient: broader colony network at t predicts higher / less-negative growth to t+1
predictor.undefined_rule: exclude intervals whose starting island total is zero

response: g_i,t+1 = log1p(N_i,t+1) - log1p(N_i,t); positive-to-zero extinction transitions retained; zero-start intervals excluded

models.C0: next_growth ~ island fixed effects + z(log1p current abundance) + z(year)

validation.scheme: leave-one-end-year-out; all islands with response ending in the held-out year are removed together

decision_rule: support requires primary_gain > 0 and full-data effective-colony-number coefficient > 0
sensitivities: replace effective colony number with log1p active positive-colony count
add previous-year island growth to C0/C1 where available
repeat on persistently extant islands CHR,COR,HUM,TOR
interpretation_boundaries: Colony topology is derived from the same census as abundance and is an internal demographic state, not an independent causal habitat measurement.
A positive result would show predictive information in within-island colony structure, not prove that habitat loss caused the next-year decline.
Colony-code definitions are treated as stable observational units; results must report code counts by island and year and flag discontinuities.
Do not tune alternative topology indices after opening the primary result; active-colony count is the only predeclared alternate.
next_gate: If supported, seek external spatial/topographic mapping of colony codes to test habitat-state causality. If unsupported, close colony-topology as a predictive mechanism and move to prey/recruitment pathways.
